work: Other: De Christo et Antichristo (Treatise on Christ and Antichrist)
ref: De Christo et Antichristo c.3 (ANF vol. 5 chapter numbering; GCS 1 chapter III; PG 10 proem cols. ca. 727-730)
greek: ὅπως ἃ πάλαι τοῖς μακαρίοις προφήταις ἀπεκάλυψεν ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγος, νῦν αὐτὸς πάλιν ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ παῖς, ὁ πάλαι μὲν λόγος ὢν, νυνὶ δὲ καὶ
greek_edition: Bonwetsch-Achelis, Hippolytus Werke I (GCS 1, Leipzig 1897), text from archive.org item hippolytuswerke01hipp (djvu OCR), file dl/gcs1_text.txt (Greek text cut off where read; continues in the edition). Cross-check PG 10 OCR shows same wording with interleaved Latin. OCR: κ/χ and θ/ϑ may be misread.
english: Do you wish then to know in what manner the Word of God, who was again the Son of God, as He was of old the Word, communicated His revelations to the blessed prophets in former times? (ANF vol. 5, CCEL text)
translator: ANF vol. 5 (Schaff ed., 1886); translator not named in the text I read
page: ANF vol. 5 p. 205 (CCEL printed page); GCS page: unknown (between running heads I-III and III-VI)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 5, Buffalo 1886 (CCEL anf05 text); GCS 1, Leipzig 1897
what_it_says: The Word of God, who was of old the Word, is 'again' the Son of God when he revealed things to the prophets.
limits: Presents the Word as Son in the economy of revelation; does not say the Son is coeternal or consubstantial. Some read 'was again the Son' as adoptionist-sounding; not resolved here.

ref: De Christo et Antichristo c.4 (ANF vol. 5); GCS 1 chapter IV
greek: ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ὁ λόγος ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ ἄσαρχος ὢν ἐνεδύσατο τὴν ἁγίαν σάρκα ἐκ τῆς ἁγίας παρθένου ὡς νυμφίος ἱμάτιον
greek_edition: Bonwetsch-Achelis, Hippolytus Werke I (GCS 1, Leipzig 1897), text from archive.org item hippolytuswerke01hipp (djvu OCR), file dl/gcs1_text.txt. OCR: GCS prints ἄσαρ-/χος split over a line break; κ/χ may be confused (printed ἔχ in places).
english: For whereas the Word of God was without flesh, He took upon Himself the holy flesh by the holy Virgin, and prepared a robe which He wove for Himself, like a bridegroom, in the sufferings of the cross... (ANF vol. 5, CCEL)
translator: ANF vol. 5 (translator not named in text read)
page: ANF vol. 5 p. 205; GCS page unknown
what_it_says: Before the incarnation the Word of God was without flesh; he took the holy flesh from the Virgin.
limits: Pre-incarnate 'Word without flesh' is compatible with Nicene Christology; ANF note marks the Greek 'ὤν' emended to 'ἦν' (footnote 13) – a textual point, not a doctrinal one.

ref: De Christo et Antichristo c.6 (ANF vol. 5); GCS 1 chapter VI
greek: Τοῦ μὲν οὖν κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὸ βασιλικὸν καὶ ἔνδοξον ὡς λέοντος προκεχηρυγμένου
greek_edition: Bonwetsch-Achelis, Hippolytus Werke I (GCS 1, Leipzig 1897), text from archive.org item hippolytuswerke01hipp (djvu OCR), file dl/gcs1_text.txt. OCR text read; the GCS apparatus notes an alternative reading at this point (υἱοῦ τοῦ H, S).
english: Now, as our Lord Jesus Christ, who is also God, was prophesied of under the figure of a lion... (ANF vol. 5, CCEL)
translator: ANF vol. 5 (translator not named in text read)
page: ANF vol. 5 p. 206; GCS page unknown
what_it_says: The Greek reads 'our Lord and Saviour Christ Jesus, the Son of God'; the ANF English renders it 'who is also God'.
limits: GROUND TRUTH MISMATCH: the Greek I read says 'Son of God' (υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ) and not explicitly 'God'. Do not cite 'Christ is God' from c.6 without checking the GCS apparatus variant or the Migne text.

ref: De Christo et Antichristo c.26 (ANF vol. 5); GCS 1 chapter XXVI
greek: τὴν ἐξουσίαν πᾶσαν τὴν παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ δεδομένην τῷ υἱῷ ἐπέδειξεν, ὃς ἐπουρανίων τε καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ καταχθονίων βασιλεὺς καὶ κριτὴς πάντων ἀποδέδεικται, ἐπουρανίων μέν, ὅτι λόγος ἐκ καρδίας πατρὸς πρὸ πάντων γεγεννημένος
greek_edition: Bonwetsch-Achelis, Hippolytus Werke I (GCS 1, Leipzig 1897), text from archive.org item hippolytuswerke01hipp (djvu OCR), file dl/gcs1_text.txt. GCS page inferred from running heads XX-XXV (p. 17) and XXV-XXIX (p. 19), i.e. p. 18; not printed in OCR.
english: He showed all power given by the Father to the Son, who is ordained Lord of things in heaven, and things on earth, and things under the earth, and Judge of all: of things in heaven, because He was born, the Word of God, before all (ages). (ANF vol. 5, CCEL)
translator: ANF vol. 5 (translator not named in text read)
page: ANF vol. 5 p. 209 (chapter 26 begins on this page)
what_it_says: The Son holds power given by the Father; as heavenly Lord he is 'the Word begotten out of the heart of the Father before all'.
limits: Greek says 'begotten out of the heart of the Father' (ἐκ καρδίας πατρὸς); the ANF English omits 'out of the heart of the Father'. Begetting 'before all' is a generation-by-will/prolation image close to the Son as Word; no 'homoousios' here.

ref: De Christo et Antichristo c.61 (ANF vol. 5); GCS 1 chapter LXI
greek: τὴν μὲν οὖν γυναῖκα τὴν περιβεβλημένην τὸν ἥλιον σαφέστατα τὴν ἐκκλησίαν ἐδήλωσεν, ἐνδεδυμένην τὸν λόγον τὸν πατρῷον ὑπὲρ ἥλιον λάμποντα
greek_edition: Bonwetsch-Achelis, Hippolytus Werke I (GCS 1, Leipzig 1897), text from archive.org item hippolytuswerke01hipp (djvu OCR), file dl/gcs1_text.txt. OCR: 'γυναῖκα' read as '„yuvalza'; κ printed as χ in places. Page: GCS p. 41 (running head LIX-LXI 41 precedes the text).
english: By the woman then clothed with the sun, he meant most manifestly the Church, endued with the Father's word, whose brightness is above the sun. (ANF vol. 5, CCEL)
translator: ANF vol. 5 (translator not named in text read)
what_it_says: The Church is clothed with 'the Father's Word' (τὸν λόγον τὸν πατρῷον).
limits: Only ecclesiological image; the ANF clause 'declared to be God and man' (p. 217) was not located in the Greek I read.

ref: Commentary on Daniel, Dan 3:92 LXX (= Theodotion 3:25), ANF 'Scholia' section 92 (i.e. 25); GCS 1 chapter XXXII; PG 10 'In Danielem' Greek with heading μθ'
greek: καὶ ἡ ὅρασις τοῦ τετάρτου ὁμοία υἱῷ θεοῦ. Εἰπέ μοι, Ναβουχοδονόσορ, πότε γὰρ εἶδες τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα υἱὸν θεοῦ τοῦτον ὁμολογήσῃς; τίς δὲ ὁ τὴν καρδίαν σου κατανύξας, ἵνα τοιοῦτον ῥῆμα ἀποφθέγξῃ; ... αὕτη ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ χεὶρ, ὅπερ ἦν ὁ λόγος, τὴν καρδίαν τούτου κατένυξεν, ἵνα ἐπιγνοὺς τοῦτον ἐν τῇ καμίνῳ δοξάσῃ
greek_edition: Bonwetsch-Achelis, Hippolytus Werke I (GCS 1, Leipzig 1897), text from archive.org item hippolytuswerke01hipp (djvu OCR), file dl/gcs1_text.txt (verified visually at p. 106 after running head '106 ΙΠΠΟΛΥΤΟΥ'). Same passage in PG 10 Greek with Latin: 'Εἰπέ μοι, Ναθουχοδονόσορ' (OCR). OCR: ϑ for θ, χ for κ, ἢ/ἡ confused.
english: And the form of the fourth is like the Son of God. Tell me, Nebuchadnezzar, when did you see the Son of God, that you should confess that this is the Son of God? And who pricked your heart... the hand of God is here, whereby the Word pricked his heart, so that he might recognise Him in the furnace, and glorify Him. (ANF vol. 5, Salmond; New Advent 0502)
page: ANF vol. 5 printed page unknown (CCEL section 'Scholia on Daniel' begins p. 186); GCS 1 p. 106
edition: ANF vol. 5 (1886) via New Advent; GCS 1 (1897)
what_it_says: Hippolytus identifies the fourth figure in the furnace with the pre-incarnate Son of God, whom Nebuchadnezzar confessed, and says 'the Word' pricked the king's heart.
limits: Pre-incarnate Son as a visible figure (theophany) is a classic Christological topic; Hippolytus here stresses that the Son was seen 'without flesh' in the furnace (ANF 'not incarnate'), a pre-incarnate-appearance reading that Arians used for subordinate Son-as-angel arguments.

ref: Commentary on Daniel, Dan 3:93 LXX (= Theod. 3:26), ANF 'Scholia' section 93 (i.e. 26); GCS 1 chapter XXXIII
greek: καὶ τῶν μὲν τριῶν τὰ ὀνόματα ἐκάλεσεν, τοῦ δὲ τετάρτου οὐχ εὗρεν ἐξειπεῖν· οὐδέπω γὰρ ἦν ἐκ τῆς παρθένου γεγενημένος ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
greek_edition: Bonwetsch-Achelis, Hippolytus Werke I (GCS 1, Leipzig 1897), text from archive.org item hippolytuswerke01hipp (djvu OCR), file dl/gcs1_text.txt (read in OCR, page unknown: between running heads 106 and 109).
english: 93 (i.e., 26). And he said, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. The three youths he thus called by name. But he found no name by which to call the fourth. For He was not yet that Jesus born of the Virgin. (ANF vol. 5, Salmond; New Advent 0502)
page: ANF vol. 5 printed page unknown (within pp. 186-191); GCS 1 page unknown
edition: ANF vol. 5 (1886) via New Advent; GCS 1 (1897)
what_it_says: The fourth figure could not be named because Jesus was not yet born of the Virgin.
limits: Used by critics to argue the Son was 'nameless' before the incarnation; the answer is that the figure is the pre-incarnate Word whose name is revealed only in the Incarnation. Commentary-level, not doctrinal.

ref: Commentary on Daniel, Dan 7:13-14 (ANF 'Interpretation' section 18); GCS 1 Daniel book IV (page unknown, between running heads 207 and 210)
greek: ἔνσαρκος δὲ ϑεὸς καὶ ἄνθρωπος, υἱὸς ϑεοῦ καὶ ἀνθρώπου
greek_edition: Bonwetsch-Achelis, Hippolytus Werke I (GCS 1, Leipzig 1897), text from archive.org item hippolytuswerke01hipp (djvu OCR), file dl/gcs1_text.txt (read in OCR; apparatus cites Dan. 7,17.18). OCR: ϑ for θ as printed.
english: ...as God incarnate and man, Son of God and Son of man—coming from heaven as the world's Judge. (ANF vol. 5, Salmond; New Advent 0502, section 18)
page: ANF vol. 5 page unknown (section 18 of 'Interpretation', pp. 179-185); GCS page unknown
edition: ANF vol. 5 (1886) via New Advent; GCS 1 (1897)
what_it_says: The coming Christ is 'God incarnate and man, Son of God and Son of man'.
limits: 'God incarnate' is an explicit God-predicate for the Son, but in a Son-and-man incarnation context; does not treat the Holy Spirit here.

greek_edition: Greek not located in this run (GCS 1 p. 'ὑποτάξ' hits near positions 644217 and 650437 not read; apparatus at 650437 cites Hippolytus via Theodoret, Dial. II, 'πρωτότοκος λόγος'). Not verified.
english: The Father, having put all things in subjection to His own Son, both things in heaven and things on earth, showed Him forth by all as the first-begotten of God, in order that, along with the Father, He might be approved the Son of God before angels... (ANF vol. 5, Salmond; New Advent 0502)
page: ANF vol. 5 page unknown; GCS page unknown
what_it_says: The Father subjected all things to the Son and showed him as first-begotten of God, 'along with the Father' approved as Son.
limits: Subjection language (cf. 1 Cor 15:28) and 'first-begotten' are the usual subordinationist hooks; the sentence also says 'along with the Father' (synkathedra-type), which the Nicene defence reads as equal honour. Greek not verified.

greek_edition: Greek not located in this run (searched for 'ἅγιος τῶν ἁγίων' / 'Μεγάλης βουλ' with no hit). Not verified.
english: And the Most Holy is none else but the Son of God alone, who, when He came and manifested Himself, said to them, The Spirit of the Lord is upon me... (ANF vol. 5, Salmond; New Advent 0502)
what_it_says: The Most Holy anointed in Dan 9:24 is 'none else but the Son of God alone'.
limits: Only identifies the Son; no Spirit or Father statement in this sentence.

ref: Fragment on Gen 49:21-26 (Blessings of the breasts and womb), ANF 'On Genesis' fragments (heading read as 'Genesis 48:3-4' preceding; exact Gen 49 heading not confirmed)
greek_edition: Greek not located in this run. The Blessings of Isaac and Jacob as a complete work were not separately read.
english: By this is meant that the true blessing from heaven is the Spirit descending through the Word upon flesh. (ANF vol. 5, New Advent 0502, Hippolytus fragment)
translator: ANF vol. 5 (translator not named in text read)
what_it_says: The Spirit descends 'through the Word upon flesh' in the blessing of the breasts and womb.
limits: Fragmentary and heading not fully confirmed; attribution to 'Blessings of Isaac and Jacob' not verified.

ref: Fragment on Gen 49 (heading not confirmed), ANF 'On Genesis' fragments
greek_edition: Greek not located in this run.
english: For as the only begotten Word of God, being God of God, emptied Himself, according to the Scriptures... took unto Himself this vile flesh, and appeared in the form of a servant, and became obedient to God the Father, even unto death... (ANF vol. 5, New Advent 0502)
translator: ANF vol. 5 (translator not named in text read)
what_it_says: The only-begotten Word, God of God, emptied himself and took flesh, and became obedient to the Father.
limits: 'Emptied himself' (kenosis) and 'obedient to God the Father' are often cited by subordinationists; the Nicene reading treats them as the economy of the human nature. Heading and Greek not verified.
